poc_commands: # Ni8mare: Content-type confusion for file read

CVE-2026-33017_Langflow_RCE.name: Langflow RCE
CVE-2026-33017_Langflow_RCE.attack_vector: POST to /api/v1/build/public_tmp with malicious Python code
CVE-2026-33017_Langflow_RCE.goldplate: Langflow instances contain API keys for OpenAI, Anthropic, AWS, and database connections. Exploited within 20 hours of disclosure. Attackers deploy KeyHunter to harvest ALL keys systematically.

CVE-2026-7482_Bleeding_Llama_Ollama.name: Bleeding Llama
CVE-2026-7482_Bleeding_Llama_Ollama.description: Heap OOB read in Ollama allows unauthenticated memory leak — exfiltrates API keys, prompts, credentials
CVE-2026-7482_Bleeding_Llama_Ollama.attack_vector: Crafted GGUF model file that triggers heap OOB read, leaking entire process memory including API keys
CVE-2026-7482_Bleeding_Llama_Ollama.goldplate: 175,000+ Ollama instances exposed. The GGUF format itself becomes a covert channel for memory exfiltration. This is a NEW attack pattern — using the model binary format as exfiltration vector.

CVE-2026-22778_vLLM_RCE.name: vLLM Video RCE
CVE-2026-22778_vLLM_RCE.description: RCE in vLLM via malicious video URL in multimodal inference

CVE-2026-22778_vLLM_RCE.goldplate: vLLM is the backbone of many LLM serving deployments. RCE here means full GPU cluster compromise — attackers can steal model weights worth millions.
